Q: Change port for Fresh (Deno) webserver A:

Now fresh use deno serve to start the server, and dev is started with vite

so there is no default config now

if you want to change the port, you should modify the deno.json , like

{
  "nodeModulesDir": "manual",
  "tasks": {
    "check": "deno fmt --check . && deno lint . && deno check",
    "dev": "vite",
    "build": "vite build",
    "start": "deno serve --port 7000 -A _fresh/server.js",
    "update": "deno run -A -r jsr:@fresh/update ."
  },
}

and modify the vite.config.ts

https://vite.dev/config/server-options

set the port or other things you want to change

Q: Finding Patterns in a Numpy Array A:

There are a couple of accepted ways of doing this. The slow one, as you pointed out, is a sliding window search. This is slow, but probably fine for small signals and templates. You don't need to hand-roll any loops to do it either, since numpy can vectorize the computation for you:

searchval = np.array(searchval)
idx = (np.lib.stride_tricks.sliding_window_view(values, searchval.shape) == searchval).all(axis=1).nonzero()[0]

A better way is probably to convolve the two arrays:

idx = (np.convolve(values, searchval[::-1], mode='valid') == (searchval**2).sum()).nonzero()[0]

This algorithm will typically be DFT-based and therefore run in O(N log N) time, with N = values.size. The only risk here is the small probability of getting false positives from how the sum is computed. For example, with searchval == [1, 2], the trigger value is 5, which can also be achieved by matching against [3, 1] in values. You can avoid this by checking only the identified elements:

tp_idx = (np.lib.stride_tricks.sliding_window_view(values, searchval.shape)[idx] == searchval).all(axis=1).nonzero()[0]
idx = idx[tp_idx]

The sliding window itself is very fast since it just creates a view into the original data. The slow part is ==, but subsetting to the candidates with [idx] reduces the search space dramatically (unless everything is a false positive).

Q: Excel change text box color based on value A:

I am assuming that you are using a User form where you need the Textbox to change color based on the information in it.

I am currently working on the same thing and I have come with the following solution:

For UserForm1 with 4 textboxes listed 1 - 4

Private Sub Textbox1_Change()
 If TextBox1.Text = "A" Then
TextBox1.BackColor = RGB(0, 32, 96)
 ElseIf TextBox1.Text = "B" Then
TextBox1.BackColor = RGB(0, 112, 192)
  ElseIf TextBox1.Text = "C" Then
TextBox1.BackColor = RGB(189, 215, 238)
  ElseIf TextBox1.Text = "D" Then
TextBox1.BackColor = RGB(0, 176, 240)
End If
End Sub

Private Sub Textbox2_Change()
 If TextBox2.Text = "A" Then
TextBox2.BackColor = RGB(0, 32, 96)
TextBox2.Font.Color = RGB(0, 0, 0)
 ElseIf TextBox2.Text = "B" Then
TextBox2.BackColor = RGB(0, 112, 192)
  ElseIf TextBox2.Text = "C" Then
TextBox2.BackColor = RGB(189, 215, 238)
  ElseIf TextBox2.Text = "D" Then
TextBox2.BackColor = RGB(0, 176, 240)
End If
End Sub

Q: Understanding evaluate function in OBIEE A:

The Evaluate function enables you to send a function to the database to evaluate and return data to OBIEE. For security purposes you must use references in the function rather than the values themselves.

For example, if I have a column "Core"."Date" which returns the date as a string and want to use the TO_DATE function of evaluate, I would issue the following evaluate expression:

EVALUATE('TO_DATE(%1,'DD-MON-YYYY') AS DATE',"Core"."Date")

Hope that helps.
